title: Implementation Possibility of Quantum Simulation for Quantum Molecular Dynamics
authors: Xingyu Zhang, Weijia Guo, Jinke Yu, Qingyong Meng
abstract: In this work, we explore the implementation possibility of quantum simulation for quantum molecular dynamics, in particular for reaction dynamics, though several implementations have already reported through quantum-classical mixed simulations ({\it Acc. Chem. Res.} {\bf 54} (2021), 4229 and {\it J. Phys. Chem. Lett.} {\bf xx} (2026), XXXX). To analyze this aspect, we examine (1) the conjugacy relation between quantum simulator and the target molecular system, (2) the wave function correspondence in quantum algorithm and classical algorithm for multi-dimensional dynamics, (3) problems arisen from real-valued classical algorithms, and finally (4) geometric phase arisen from the separation among the degrees of freedom (DOFs). As is well known, the aforementioned first and second points play fundamental roles in quantum simulation of quantum many-body systems, and the third and fourth points are theoretical issues that might introduce problems in classical and quantum computing. In this work, we mainly focus on the third and fourth points by analysis of the first two points by reviewing previously reported quantum-classical mixed implementations of quantum simulation. We also consider gauge freedom in high-dimensional quantum molecular dynamics that has been introduced recently, and then discuss possibility of advantages and disadvantages of quantum simulation for molecular reaction dynamics.
summary: This paper investigates the theoretical possibility of using quantum simulation for quantum molecular dynamics, particularly for chemical reactions. It critically analyzes underlying mathematical requirements, focusing on issues like the conjugacy between systems and the implications of real-valued quantum mechanics. The work provides a theoretical roadmap for advancing quantum simulation in chemistry.
main_problem: The paper explores the theoretical feasibility of using quantum simulation techniques to model complex quantum molecular dynamics, especially for chemical reaction processes.
main_result: The authors analyze fundamental theoretical hurdles, such as the conjugacy relation between dynamical systems, the transition to real-valued quantum mechanics, and the emergence of geometric phases from degrees of freedom separation.
method: The analysis reviews existing quantum-classical mixed simulation implementations and focuses on theoretical constraints by examining the mathematical requirements for simulating time evolution.
model_or_system: The focus is on quantum many-body systems undergoing molecular reaction dynamics. The theoretical framework involves comparing the target molecular system's dynamics with the dynamics implemented on a quantum simulator.
key_observables: Population fractions ($P_0$), rate constants ($k$), and the general time evolution of the quantum state.
important_parameters: The separation of degrees of freedom (DOFs) and the resulting geometric phase ambiguity are key theoretical parameters.
main_assumptions: The paper assumes the necessity of a conjugacy relation for successful simulation and discusses the theoretical implications of using real-valued quantum mechanics instead of complex Hilbert spaces.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate various quantum algorithms (VQE, qEOM) and model results, such as the time evolution of the Marcus spin-boson model showing charge transfer regimes.
paper_structure: The paper is structured theoretically, analyzing four key aspects (conjugacy, wave function correspondence, real-valued issues, geometric phase) by reviewing existing quantum-classical mixed implementations.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the theoretical limits and necessary mathematical foundations for applying quantum computation to simulate fundamental processes in molecular physics and chemical dynamics.
